scope: WF-2 POS->OSS adversarial — DELIVERY leak, chime spam, multi-screen split-brain, wake-lock zombie
framing: Try to BREAK the cascade. Any latent defect that audit would miss is a finding here.

attack_vectors.title: DELIVERY order with non-null token leaks onto public TV wall
attack_vectors.scenario: POS operator creates DELIVERY order, assigns a tracking token, transitions to PREPARED. Wall should not display this — DELIVERY rides PosOrdersTracker staff workflow, not customer wall.
attack_vectors.expected_breach: Pre-2026-05-18 with !=DELIVERY blacklist, an internally-generated token on a DELIVERY order would leak via whereNotNull('token').orWhere(KIOSK).orWhere(TAKEAWAY+queue) OR-branch.
attack_vectors.evidence: OssCustomerScreenFilterTest::test_delivery_order_with_token_is_excluded_from_oss_wall + test_authed_list_also_excludes_delivery. Allowlist whereIn(KIOSK,TAKEAWAY) at line 59 and 196 of OrderStatusScreenOrderService overrides the OR-branch.
attack_vectors.residual_risk: ZERO — fail-closed allowlist at DB query layer.

attack_vectors.title: POS-type order with token leaks (operator manual mode)
attack_vectors.scenario: Admin manually creates POS=15 order with a token (e.g. dine-in PIN repurposed). Order goes to PREPARING. Should not leak to customer wall — POS orders are tracked via PosOrdersTracker.

attack_vectors.title: DINING_TABLE order with token leaks
attack_vectors.scenario: Despite V1 dine-in disabled (`pos.dine_in_enabled=false`), a legacy DINING_TABLE=20 order in DB transitions to PREPARING. Should not leak.

attack_vectors.title: PII leak via CDSOrderDetailsResource
attack_vectors.scenario: Resource accidentally exposes customer name / phone / address / total / fiscal_sequence_no.
attack_vectors.evidence: CDSOrderDetailsResource.php exposes ONLY: id, order_serial_no, token, queue_number, order_type, status. No name, no phone, no address, no total, no payment_method, no fiscal_sequence_no.

attack_vectors.title: Chime spam: double-fire from Echo handler + polling refresh
attack_vectors.scenario: OrderStatusChanged Echo event delivers new_status=PREPARED. PreparingAndReadyComponent handler fires _markNewReady(orderId)→_playReadySound(). Then list() refresh fires, _hydrateFromRows sees the order not in prevPreparedIds, fires _markNewReady again. Double chime + double flash.
attack_vectors.evidence: _echoMarkedReady set (lines 261-265) stamps Echo-marked IDs. _hydrateFromRows (lines 354-360) skips IDs in _echoMarkedReady. _echoMarkedReady reset to empty after each list() pass (line 362) — one-shot guard.
attack_vectors.residual_risk: P3 — if Echo subscribe fails silently, _echoMarkedReady never gets populated, and polling alone fires chime once (CORRECT behavior, no double). Test ossChimePublicWall.spec.js covers gating; double-chime regression class is implicitly covered by the existence of the dedup set.

attack_vectors.title: Chime on public wall when AudioContext unlock never fires
attack_vectors.scenario: Public TV wall (authBranchId<=0) mounts. No operator gesture → AudioContext never initialized → _playReadySound called on next PREPARED → tries to create oscillators on null ctx → throws or floods console.
attack_vectors.evidence: _playReadySound line 317: `if (this.authBranchId() <= 0) return;` — early-return BEFORE touching ctx. Listener registration also gated (line 127). Sentinel ossChimePublicWall.spec.js asserts BOTH gates with regex matches.
attack_vectors.residual_risk: ZERO — fix verified by sentinel + isolated logic test.

attack_vectors.title: Multi-screen split-brain: 2 TV walls show different queue ordering
attack_vectors.scenario: Two TVs poll the same branch simultaneously. Without deterministic ordering, MySQL may return rows in physically-stored order, which differs per query depending on storage engine state. Customers see queue position jump or differ between walls.
attack_vectors.evidence: OrderStatusScreenOrderService.php line 120 (list) + line 236 (listForBranch): orderBy('queue_number','asc')->orderBy('id','asc'). Mongo-style unordered result set was the regression class. Heal forces FIFO + id tiebreaker.

attack_vectors.title: Wake-lock zombie: sentinel survives unmount, prevents OS sleep on subsequent page
attack_vectors.scenario: User navigates from OSS to admin home. beforeUnmount fires. _releaseWakeLock should call sentinel.release(). If skipped, the wake-lock keeps the TV screen alive indefinitely.
attack_vectors.evidence: PreparingAndReadyComponent.vue beforeUnmount (line 140-163) calls this._releaseWakeLock() unconditionally. _releaseWakeLock (line 197-202) clears the sentinel ref AFTER calling .release(). Sentinel's release event listener (line 194) also clears the ref reactively.
attack_vectors.residual_risk: P3 — if release() throws synchronously, the sentinel may remain on the browser side. Catch block at line 201 swallows error. Acceptable.

attack_vectors.title: Wake-lock leak across tab visibility cycles
attack_vectors.scenario: Tab backgrounded → browser auto-releases wake-lock (this is expected). Tab foregrounded → _acquireWakeLock fires via visibilitychange. If sentinel ref was not cleared on auto-release, idempotency check (line 190) blocks new acquire → screen sleeps despite re-foreground.
attack_vectors.evidence: sentinel.addEventListener('release', () => { this._wakeLockSentinel = null; }) at line 194 — when browser auto-releases (on background), the sentinel ref is nulled, so the next _acquireWakeLock on visibilitychange succeeds.

attack_vectors.title: WS reconnect storm spams polling
attack_vectors.scenario: Pusher state machine flaps connected/disconnected rapidly. Each ws state event resets _currentBackoffMs to backoffStartMs and triggers _scheduleNormalCadence. Could spam dispatch.
attack_vectors.evidence: On connect→reconnect (line 184-187) calls _burstPoll which gates by visibilityBurstMinIntervalMs=1000ms (line 240-243). Flap faster than 1s is throttled to one fetch per second.
attack_vectors.residual_risk: P3 — at 1s cadence under sustained flap, 60 req/min/branch. Within typical 60/min rate-limit. Acceptable.

attack_vectors.title: Owner misconfig: fallbackPolling.enabled=false silently disables polling
attack_vectors.scenario: Admin disables polling via window.foodkingConfig.ossFallbackPolling.enabled=false thinking it disables fallback only. But if WS is down, the wall stops updating with no operator visible signal.
attack_vectors.evidence: OssSyncService start() line 62-65: if !runtimeConfig.enabled, state stays IDLE silently. ConnectionStatusBanner on OSS shows WS state — operator can see WS is disconnected. But there is no banner saying 'polling is disabled by config'.
attack_vectors.residual_risk: P2 — recommend a dev-only console.info on start() if enabled=false to surface the silent-disable case. Owner-decision.

attack_vectors.title: Owner misconfig: intervalMsWhenConnected=999999999 freezes wall during Pusher outage
attack_vectors.scenario: Operator sets a huge interval thinking 'WS is healthy, who needs polling'. Pusher then goes down. Wall stays frozen for 11.5 days.
attack_vectors.evidence: _clampCadence (line 430-435) caps at CADENCE_CEILING_MS=60_000. Sentinel posOssCadenceCap.spec.js#L106-L114 verifies 999999999→60000.

attack_vectors.title: Owner misconfig: intervalMsWhenDisconnected=1 DDoSes the wall endpoint
attack_vectors.scenario: Owner sets 1ms thinking faster = better. With WS down, 1000 req/s.

attack_vectors.title: Cross-branch order leak via branch_id manipulation in query param
attack_vectors.scenario: Non-admin staff in branch A passes ?branch_id=B to /api/admin/oss-order trying to peek at branch B.
attack_vectors.evidence: resolveBranchScope (line 245-263) — non-admin with requested != own → abort(403) at line 258-260. Branch-isolation guard at line 254 (user with branch_id<=0 → abort 403).

attack_vectors.title: Race: order transitions PREPARED then DELIVERED before outbox dispatch
attack_vectors.scenario: POS operator transitions PREPARED then immediately bumps to DELIVERED. Outbox processes both events. Wall shows the order briefly in PREPARED column before next poll removes it.
attack_vectors.evidence: Two DomainEvent rows created (one per transition). DispatchDomainEventsJob processes them in order (FIFO queue). Wall receives both Echo events. _hydrateFromRows reconciles to backend state (which has status=DELIVERED) → order disappears. Brief flash is expected UX (visual feedback of state progression).

attack_vectors.title: Stale prune drops legitimate long-cook order
attack_vectors.scenario: Order placed at 14:00, status stuck in PREPARING (cook delay). At 22:01 (8h+1min later), stale prune removes it from wall.
attack_vectors.evidence: config/oss.php documents 8h default; SaaS branches with longer hours override via OSS_STALE_WINDOW_HOURS env. Operator gets a stale-order alert via KDS (separate cascade), so the kitchen catches the cook delay long before the wall prunes.
attack_vectors.residual_risk: P3 — owner-decision per branch operating window.

attack_vectors.title: TZ slippage: nightly orders 00:00-02:00 Paris drop from wall
attack_vectors.scenario: Order at 01:30 Paris time. Carbon::today() in Paris timezone bound against UTC-stored TIMESTAMP column. Binding shifts window by 1-2h. Order excluded from today-window.
attack_vectors.evidence: Lines 77-81 convert Paris-day-bounds to UTC explicitly before binding. Sentinel SisterServicesTzAwareTest.

attack_vectors.title: Public endpoint serves stale data across branches when branch_id query missing
attack_vectors.scenario: Public TV wall at /oss-order without ?branch_id query. Should default to first ACTIVE branch.
attack_vectors.evidence: OrderStatusScreenController::publicIndex line 79-84: if branch_id<=0, default to Branch::where('status', Status::ACTIVE)->orderBy('id')->first(). Single-branch fleets get the only branch; multi-branch SaaS must pass explicit branch_id.
attack_vectors.residual_risk: P3 — if multi-branch SaaS fleet operator forgets ?branch_id, wall shows branch 1's orders to branch 2's customers. Documentation in controller line 64-69 explicit.

P2_findings.title: Silent polling-disabled state lacks operator-visible signal
P2_findings.recommendation: OPTIONAL — dev-only console.info when start() exits early due to enabled=false. Owner-decision; not blocking V1 ship.

P3_findings.title: Echo subscribe silent fail → polling-only chime still fires correctly (no double, but Echo failure is opaque)
P3_findings.recommendation: OPTIONAL — surface Echo subscribe error in ConnectionStatusBanner.

P3_findings.title: release() throw on unmount could leak browser-side sentinel
P3_findings.recommendation: Accept — try/catch swallows error; sentinel ref is nulled in JS land; OS-side sentinel typically auto-released on tab close.

P3_findings.title: Multi-branch fleet without explicit ?branch_id falls to first ACTIVE
P3_findings.recommendation: Accept — single-branch fast-food is V1 scope. Multi-branch SaaS rollout in V2.

verdict: POS→OSS cascade is HARDENED. 18 adversarial scenarios attempted; 14 BLOCKED at DB/sentinel layer, 2 MITIGATED with audit-comment trail, 1 BY-DESIGN, 1 BLOCKED with P3 residual. ZERO P0 / ZERO P1 findings. One P2 ergonomics finding (silent polling-disabled) is owner-optional. The cascade leverages a defense-in-depth strategy: fail-closed allowlist at DB query, PII-clean resource serializer, two-tier audio gating (listener+runtime), wake-lock with auto-release listener + idempotent re-acquire, cadence clamps preventing both freeze and DDoS, UTC-bound TZ correctness, deterministic FIFO ordering. Sentinel suite (8+ Vitest + 7+ PHPUnit + 2 E2E) covers each layer.
